podcast.body: This song appeared on the "Manic Hedgehog tape" in October 1991. It was re-recorded and released as a single in February 1993, following "Creep." Radiohead frequently used it to open their live sets, where it was well-received. It became Radiohead's first top 40 hit in the UK, peaking at number 32 on the British charts. "It was Anyone Can Play Guitar, which reached number 32 on the British charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is referenced in connection with the invention of the quarter-inch funnel plug by George Koi, which made connecting guitars (and other instruments/equipment) much easier and ubiquitous, thus enabling more people to play music. The phrase "anyone can play guitar" directly references the song title. "And now, thanks to George, anyone can play guitar."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
